bib.title: $δ$-mem: Efficient Online Memory for Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "δ-mem: Efficient Online Memory For Large Language Models", Jingdi Lei, Di Zhang (equal contribution), Junxian Li, Weida Wang, Kaixuan Fan, Xiang Liu, Qihan Liu, Xiaoteng Ma, Baian Chen, Soujanya Poria (corresponding). Affiliations: NTU, Fudan, SJTU, CUHK, HKUST(GZ), Mind Lab. Header says "40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)"; arXiv:2605.12357v2, cs.AI, 28 Sep 2026. Code: github.com/declare-lab/delta-Mem.
COVERAGE: all 15 of 15 pages, 54,285 chars, including limitations and appendices A-E. References skimmed only. No extraction faults, no embedded instructions.

MAIN CLAIM: A frozen full-attention backbone plus a tiny fixed-size matrix state (8x8) can serve as memory. The state is updated by a gated delta rule. Its readout is turned into low-rank corrections to the query and output of attention. It beats text, parametric and outside-channel memory baselines on average, with no context extension.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (all Qwen3-4B-Instruct unless stated; Table 1, p6)
1. Average over IFEval, HotpotQA (EM), GPQA-D, MemoryAgentBench and LoCoMo: backbone 46.79, best non-δ-mem baseline Context2LoRA 44.90, δ-mem TSW 51.66 (SSW 51.44, MSW 50.74). The abstract's "1.10x backbone, 1.15x strongest non-δ-mem baseline" matches these figures. The two ratios are computed from the 51.66 average.
2. Memory-heavy tasks: MemoryAgentBench avg 29.54 -> 38.85 (MSW); LoCoMo avg 40.79 -> 49.12 (MSW). TTL subtask 26.14 -> 50.50 (SSW). Both the abstract and the text give "1.31x" and "1.20x" for these.
3. Other backbones (Table 2, p7): Qwen3-8B 47.20 -> 50.86 (SSW); SmolLM3-3B 26.08 -> 36.96 (MSW). Gains shrink on the stronger model.
4. Context recovery (Fig 2, p8): with the history removed and only the 8x8 state injected, HotpotQA EM goes 0.08 -> 6.48 and F1 8.27 -> 15.20. LoCoMo avg goes 3.49 -> 8.05. The state recovers only a small part of the lost context.
Overhead (App. E, p15): 4.87M trainable params (0.12% of the backbone) for SSW and TSW, 19.47M (0.48%) for MSW. MLP Memory needs 3078M (76.40%). Training: 1 epoch on 2,219 QASPER samples, r=8, alpha=16, applied to the q and o branches only, 8xA800, seed 42.
Baselines in Table 1 (same backbone): BM25 RAG 44.56, LLMLingua-2 42.96, MemoryBank 43.88, MemGen 30.66, MLP Memory 22.85. Every text-memory baseline scores below the backbone's 46.79. BM25 RAG on HotpotQA EM goes 42.35 -> 40.35.

QUOTES
- "δ-mem compresses past information into a fixed-size state matrix updated by delta-rule learning, and uses its readout to generate low-rank corrections to the backbone's attention computation during generation." (p1, abstract)
- "Textual memory methods show inconsistent gains, likely due to retrieval noise and information loss introduced by compressing memory into token space." (p7). This is the authors' hypothesis, not a tested result.

LIMITS
- The authors concede two things (App. A, p14). The compact state approximates explicit context, and full-context fidelity is future work. Per-step state updates slow decoding; the paper reports throughput below Vanilla and Context2LoRA (Fig 3a) but faster than MemGen. No exact slowdown figure is in the extracted text.
- Not shown: any model above 8B. A single seed (42) is used, with no variance or confidence intervals reported. Test-set sizes are not stated in the extracted text. Training is on one small dataset (QASPER). Only three small backbones are tested, and no head-to-head against Mem0-style or agentic text memory with a strong retriever.
- Trained SFT modules are tied to the specific backbone. The "no explicit context" claim rests on the no-context ablation, which recovers only 6.48 EM.
- Some Table 1 baselines (BM25 RAG, LLMLingua-2, MemoryBank) lack IFEval and GPQA entries, so the "strongest baseline" average comparison covers fewer cells for them.
- Qwen3-8B gain is modest (+3.66). The writing strategy that wins varies by backbone (SSW, TSW or MSW).
- The privacy and stale-memory risks of persistent memory are noted in App. B.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- Delta-rule gated retention, inspired by Qwen-Next (Yang et al. 2025, Qwen3 report).
- Text memory: RAG (Lewis et al. 2020), MemGPT (Packer 2023), MemoryBank (Zhong 2024 AAAI), LLMLingua-2 (Pan 2024 ACL Findings), Mem0 (Chhikara 2025).
- Latent or outside-channel: Memorizing Transformers (Wu et al. 2022), LongMem (Wang et al. 2023 NeurIPS), MLP Memory (Wei 2026).
- Parametric: LoRA (Hu et al. 2022), Prefix-Tuning (Li & Liang 2021), ROME (Meng 2022), MEMIT (2022), MemGen (Zhang 2025).
- Closest architectures: Infini-attention (Munkhdalai 2024), Titans (Behrouz 2024), NHA, Hymba, NAtS-L.
- Context rot (Hong et al. 2025, Chroma).
- Benchmarks: HotpotQA (2018), LoCoMo (2024), MemoryAgentBench (Hu et al. 2025), IFEval, GPQA.

FIGURE CANDIDATE
Figure 1 (p3): architecture overview showing the read of the old state, the q/o steering, the delta-rule write, and the three write granularities (TSW, SSW, MSW). It is the best single picture of "memory in attention". Alternative: Figure 2 (p8), a bar chart of the no-context baseline against the 8x8 state recovery.

KEY EQUATION (p4, Eq. 10): S_t = Diag(λ_t) S_{t-1} + Diag(β_t)(v_t − S_{t-1} k_t) k_t^T. Read: r_t = S_{t-1} q_t. Corrections: Δq = W_Δq r_t, Δo = W_Δo r_t. Read cost is independent of history length.

PROBLEMS: None. The extracted table values are run together in places, so I used the printed averages and the text's own sentences.
